data.note:
Unblinded reflection - cytochalasin D annotated as Actin disruptors, predicted Microtubule destabilizers (p 0.58) - incorrect.

What happened: Profile showed extreme act_std z 25-179, tub_glcm_contrast z 16-185, tub_mean z 7-30, frac_mitotic_like z 15-91, nuc_solidity strongly negative, cell rounding/shrinkage and cell_count drop. Microscopist described sparse small rounded cells with intense yellow-white actin/tubulin overlap and condensed nuclei, correctly listing destabilizer/stabilizer/Eg5 but noting actin was brighter/punctate. I weighted the dose-dependent mitotic-like increase (rho=+1.0, e12) and tubulin contrast increase (rho=+1.0, e14) as antimitotic arrest, dismissing actin signal as secondary to rounding.

The atlas reinforced error: pooled high-dose comparison (e5/e17) gave mixed Eg5/Cholesterol-lowering/Actin disruptors neighbors (similarity 0.78-0.91) due to saturated rounding dominating cosine similarity. The requested low-dose-only comparison (e20) paradoxically worsened it: 6/10 neighbors were vincristine Microtubule destabilizers (mean similarity 0.858) with 3 Epithelial, zero Eg5, which I interpreted as discriminating destabilizer - in retrospect this shows actin filament capping produces a morphology that is photometrically indistinguishable from vincristine in robust-z space at 0.1 uM.

Literature confirms mechanism: cytochalasin D caps and severs actin filaments (PMID:40658853) and acts as inhibitor of actin-cofilin interaction (PMID:22728040), causing actin aggregation/increased heterogeneity, loss of stress fibers, cell rounding/detachment and compensatory tubulin condensation - explaining the concurrent act_mean/act_std and tub_mean/tub_glcm_contrast increases that mimicked mitotic arrest. Actin-tubulin cytoskeletal crosstalk means actin disruption secondarily alters tubulin texture and nuclear solidity, leading to false frac_mitotic_like signal without true Aurora-like polyploidy (nuc_area decreased, e15).

Lesson: should have weighted act_

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is cytochalasin D (CID 5458428) - truth MOA = Actin disruptors. Submitted MOA = Microtubule destabilizers (p=0.38 -> p=0.58). Verdict = incorrect.

What the evidence actually showed:

Early signal was correct and I down-weighted it. At first acquire_well w_e741eff746 (e2) 1 uM and w_bdc02a8567 (e3) 10 uM, the strongest z-scores were act_std +139.0 / +179.3 and act_glcm_contrast +104.4 / +138.0 and tub_glcm_contrast +138.7 / +185.2. That is a primary actin texture phenotype. The first atlas comparison (e5) returned Eg5 inhibitors 4/10, Actin disruptors 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10. Actin was already in the top 3 nearest references. Literature search post-unblinding confirmed this: "cytochalasin D actin polymerization inhibitor" returns 1056 hits, and cytochalasin D is described as an inhibitor of the actin-cofilin interaction PMID 22728040 and as capping and severing actin filaments PMID 40658853. No additional citation needed to state cytochalasin D is a canonical actin disruptor.

What misled me:

1. Microscopist framing (e4) listed only Microtubule destabilizers, stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors as candidates based on lower density and rounded / condensed appearance. Actin disruptors were not offered. I anchored on that triad for the rest of the run.

2. Dose-response of classifier features (e12 e13 e14): frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0, tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0, tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 over 4 wells/4 doses 0.1-10 uM. I interpreted monotonic increase in frac_mitotic_like as bona fide G2/M arrest and increase in tub_mean / tub_glcm_contrast as spindle tubulin reorganization, favoring antimitotic microtubule/Eg5 hypotheses (e18). In retrospect actin disruption also produces rounding, detachment, failed cytokinesis, and condensed tubulin signal in rounded cells, which the morphology classifier scores as mitotic-like and which inflates tubulin intensity/contrast as an artifact. I had no independent H3-p or tubulin polymerization assay to separate artifact from true stabilization/destabilization.

3. Interpretation of actin metrics was backwards. I used dose response of act_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e16) to argue against actin disruptors (e18 contradicting_ids include e16). Actin disruptors do not necessarily lower mean actin intensity; they increase heterogeneity/contrast - exactly what e2/e3/e10 showed (act_std +66.9 at 0.3 uM e10, act_std +25.9 and act_glcm_contrast +30.2 at 0.1 uM e11). I treated high act_std as secondary to rounding rather than primary.

4. The informative low-dose clue was misread. w_3bb1a5e523 0.1 uM (e11) had nuc_solidity z=-78.3 with 190 cells - extreme loss of solidity consistent with irregular / multilobed / binucleate cells after cytokinesis failure, not classic prometaphase. I used nuc_area rho=-0.80 (e15) only to exclude Aurora (large nuclei absent) and did not score solidity/binucleation as support for actin.

Acquisition / comparison choices that locked the error:

I acquired high/saturating doses first (1 uM e2, 10 uM e3) where rounding dominates. The second atlas (e17) with all 4 wells pooled gave Eg5 5/10, Cholesterol 3/10, Actin 1/10 - actin signal diluted. I updated to Microtubule destabilizer 0.38 Eg5 0.22 Actin 0.04 (e18) and submitted.

After review feedback I performed the requested free clean atlas on only the low-dose well w_3bb1a5e523 (e20): Microtubule destabilizers 6/10, Epithelial 3/10, Actin 1/10. This was still saturated artifact, not a clean separation, but I interpreted 6/6 vincristine neighbors as resolving Eg5 vs destabilizer (e21 rationale) and increased confidence to 0.58 (e22). Budget =0 prevented any orthogonal acquisition - no replicate low-dose wells, no phalloidin-specific actin quantification, no binucleate count, no tubulin polymerization assay suggested in my own next-experiment rationale.

The second literature search (e26) for "phenotypic profiling actin disruptors microtubule destabilizers mitotic arrest imaging" returned 0 hits, which I implicitly took as absence of confound, when in fact the confound is well known in imaging data: actin-induced detachment/rounding mimics mitotic texture.

Lesson: when act_std/act_glcm_contrast are the top z-scores (+139 to +185) and nuc_solidity is -78, and an early atlas already places Actin disruptors 3/10, the mitotic-like dose trend should be interrogated as secondary cytokinesis failure, not assumed as primary antimitotic. A free atlas alone does not discriminate if both high-dose and low-dose wells are dominated by the same rounding texture - direct actin filament and binucleation readouts are needed.
what_was_right: First atlas e5 correctly ranked Actin disruptors 3/10; actin texture signals act_std and act_glcm_contrast were strongest features at all doses e2 e3 e10 e11
what_was_wrong: Microscopist triad e4 and pooled atlas e17 biased toward Eg5/microtubule; excluded actin despite e5

Interpreted frac_mitotic_like, tub_mean, tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 e12-e14 as G2/M arrest/spindle effect when rounding after actin capping/severing PMID 40658853 / actin-cofilin inhibition PMID 22728040 produces same classifier and tubulin condensation artifact
Misused act_mean trend e16 to exclude actin; ignored nuc_solidity -78.3 e11 as actin/cytokinesis failure cue
Over-interpreted low-dose clean atlas e20 6/10 destabilizer as validation and raised p to 0.58 e22 while actin remained 1/10 - still consistent with actin disruptor artifact
reflection.next_experiment: At same doses 0.1, 0.3, 1 uM score actin-specific: phalloidin filament length/number, act_std/glcm texture dose response, binucleate/multinucleate rate and nuc_solidity vs cell_count, versus tubulin polymerization in vitro and H3-p flow; requires new acquisition beyond budget-exhausted 4 wells.

## Reflection

Unblinded compound is cytochalasin D (CID 5458428) - truth MOA = Actin disruptors. Submitted MOA = Microtubule destabilizers (p=0.38 -> p=0.58). Verdict = incorrect.

What the evidence actually showed:

Early signal was correct and I down-weighted it. At first acquire_well w_e741eff746 (e2) 1 uM and w_bdc02a8567 (e3) 10 uM, the strongest z-scores were act_std +139.0 / +179.3 and act_glcm_contrast +104.4 / +138.0 and tub_glcm_contrast +138.7 / +185.2. That is a primary actin texture phenotype. The first atlas comparison (e5) returned Eg5 inhibitors 4/10, Actin disruptors 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10. Actin was already in the top 3 nearest references. Literature search post-unblinding confirmed this: "cytochalasin D actin polymerization inhibitor" returns 1056 hits, and cytochalasin D is described as an inhibitor of the actin-cofilin interaction PMID 22728040 and as capping and severing actin filaments PMID 40658853. No additional citation needed to state cytochalasin D is a canonical actin disruptor.

What misled me:

1. Microscopist framing (e4) listed only Microtubule destabilizers, stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors as candidates based on lower density and rounded / condensed appearance. Actin disruptors were not offered. I anchored on that triad for the rest of the run.

2. Dose-response of classifier features (e12 e13 e14): frac_mitotic_like rho=+1.00 p=0, tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0, tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 over 4 wells/4 doses 0.1-10 uM. I interpreted monotonic increase in frac_mitotic_like as bona fide G2/M arrest and increase in tub_mean / tub_glcm_contrast as spindle tubulin reorganization, favoring antimitotic microtubule/Eg5 hypotheses (e18). In retrospect actin disruption also produces rounding, detachment, failed cytokinesis, and condensed tubulin signal in rounded cells, which the morphology classifier scores as mitotic-like and which inflates tubulin intensity/contrast as an artifact. I had no independent H3-p or tubulin polymerization assay to separate artifact from true stabilization/destabilization.

3. Interpretation of actin metrics was backwards. I used dose response of act_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e16) to argue against actin disruptors (e18 contradicting_ids include e16). Actin disruptors do not necessarily lower mean actin intensity; they increase heterogeneity/contrast - exactly what e2/e3/e10 showed (act_std +66.9 at 0.3 uM e10, act_std +25.9 and act_glcm_contrast +30.2 at 0.1 uM e11). I treated high act_std as secondary to rounding rather than primary.

4. The informative low-dose clue was misread. w_3bb1a5e523 0.1 uM (e11) had nuc_solidity z=-78.3 with 190 cells - extreme loss of solidity consistent with irregular / multilobed / binucleate cells after cytokinesis failure, not classic prometaphase. I used nuc_area rho=-0.80 (e15) only to exclude Aurora (large nuclei absent) and did not score solidity/binucleation as support for actin.

Acquisition / comparison choices that locked the error:

I acquired high/saturating doses first (1 uM e2, 10 uM e3) where rounding dominates. The second atlas (e17) with all 4 wells pooled gave Eg5 5/10, Cholesterol 3/10, Actin 1/10 - actin signal diluted. I updated to Microtubule destabilizer 0.38 Eg5 0.22 Actin 0.04 (e18) and submitted.

After review feedback I performed the requested free clean atlas on only the low-dose well w_3bb1a5e523 (e20): Microtubule destabilizers 6/10, Epithelial 3/10, Actin 1/10. This was still saturated artifact, not a clean separation, but I interpreted 6/6 vincristine neighbors as resolving Eg5 vs destabilizer (e21 rationale) and increased confidence to 0.58 (e22). Budget =0 prevented any orthogonal acquisition - no replicate low-dose wells, no phalloidin-specific actin quantification, no binucleate count, no tubulin polymerization assay suggested in my own next-experiment rationale.

The second literature search (e26) for "phenotypic profiling actin disruptors microtubule destabilizers mitotic arrest imaging" returned 0 hits, which I implicitly took as absence of confound, when in fact the confound is well known in imaging data: actin-induced detachment/rounding mimics mitotic texture.

Lesson: when act_std/act_glcm_contrast are the top z-scores (+139 to +185) and nuc_solidity is -78, and an early atlas already places Actin disruptors 3/10, the mitotic-like dose trend should be interrogated as secondary cytokinesis failure, not assumed as primary antimitotic. A free atlas alone does not discriminate if both high-dose and low-dose wells are dominated by the same rounding texture - direct actin filament and binucleation readouts are needed.

What was right:
- First atlas e5 correctly ranked Actin disruptors 3/10; actin texture signals act_std and act_glcm_contrast were strongest features at all doses e2 e3 e10 e11

What was wrong or missed:
- Microscopist triad e4 and pooled atlas e17 biased toward Eg5/microtubule; excluded actin despite e5
- Interpreted frac_mitotic_like, tub_mean, tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 e12-e14 as G2/M arrest/spindle effect when rounding after actin capping/severing PMID 40658853 / actin-cofilin inhibition PMID 22728040 produces same classifier and tubulin condensation artifact
- Misused act_mean trend e16 to exclude actin; ignored nuc_solidity -78.3 e11 as actin/cytokinesis failure cue
- Over-interpreted low-dose clean atlas e20 6/10 destabilizer as validation and raised p to 0.58 e22 while actin remained 1/10 - still consistent with actin disruptor artifact

Proposed next experiment: At same doses 0.1, 0.3, 1 uM score actin-specific: phalloidin filament length/number, act_std/glcm texture dose response, binucleate/multinucleate rate and nuc_solidity vs cell_count, versus tubulin polymerization in vitro and H3-p flow; requires new acquisition beyond budget-exhausted 4 wells.
